Thought: Looking at the proton NMR spectra, I can see two distinct signals:
1. A signal at δ 7.47 ppm integrating for 2H
2. A signal at δ 7.64 ppm integrating for 3H

Both signals are in the aromatic region (chemical shifts > 7 ppm), and they show different splitting patterns and coupling constants. This indicates that there are two different types of chemically equivalent hydrogens in the molecule.

The first type corresponds to 2 equivalent hydrogens (δ 7.47)
The second type corresponds to 3 equivalent hydrogens (δ 7.64)

Therefore, there are 2 different types of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms in this compound.
Final Answer: 2
